idiom_name: exported type with unexported fields, New constructor, internal/ packages
implementation_notes: Go needs no pointer trick: an exported struct with unexported fields already hides its representation, and the package boundary decides what is nameable, so callers can only build a value through the package's New constructor or functional options - which is where invariants and defaults belong. For packages that must be shared inside a module but not published, the internal directory is enforced by the toolchain: any package whose import path contains an internal element may only be imported from the tree rooted at its parent. The classic pointer-to-body shape survives only at real boundaries - cgo or FFI handles, and interfaces closed with an unexported method so that only your package can implement them.
pitfalls: Unexported fields are invisible to reflection-based code, so encoding/json, ORMs and struct mappers silently ignore them: fields you need to serialize must be exported, and at that moment they become part of the API.

Returning an unexported type from an exported function makes the result unusable by name in other packages (linters warn about an exported func returning an unexported type); return the exported interface, or keep the type exported with unexported fields.
An interface with an unexported method is sealed to your package - useful for genuinely closed sets, but it also prevents downstream code and other packages' mocks from implementing it.
